comparison: Perfect agreement on crosslinking methodology (C27-C33). Both evaluations support the experimental design with specific residue positions and crosslinking efficiency measurements. Reviewers accept the approach without criticism.

Perfect agreement on steady-state ATPase measurements (C34-C39). Both evaluations support the data showing crosslinks reduce kcat. Peer reviewers note the work is 'technically rigorous' and 'biochemically rigorous.'

Perfect agreement on E236A mutant characterization (C48-C54). Both evaluations support the stopped-flow and smFRET measurements. Peer reviewers accept this characterization as establishing properties needed for heterodimer experiments.

Perfect agreement on structural interpretation (C105-C109). Both evaluations support integration of kinetic results with cryo-EM and crystal structure data. Peer reviewers note consistency with structural work, though Reviewer 3 suggests direct structural validation would strengthen conclusions.

Both support pre-steady-state ATP binding/dissociation kinetics (C40-C47 overlap with C44-C45, C47). OpenEval emphasizes differential effects on rear vs front head crosslinks. Peer reviewers affirm findings are 'well supported by experimental data.'

Both support ATP kinetics measurements (C40-C47 overlap with C42-C43, C46). OpenEval details stopped-flow experiments showing rear head crosslink dramatically reduces k-1. Peer reviewers confirm neck-linker conformation reduces ATP dissociation rate.

Both support rear head ATP off-rate measurements (C75-C78). OpenEval emphasizes 42-fold difference vs E236A monomer as evidence for strain-dependent gating. Peer reviewers unanimously support findings on ATP dissociation rate reduction.

Both support microtubule dissociation measurements (C55-C59 overlap with C55, C57-C58). OpenEval notes complementary methods (light scattering and SMF) strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers confirm front head reduces detachment rates.

Both support front head detachment measurements (C79-C84 overlap with C83-C84). OpenEval emphasizes convergent evidence from heterodimer and crosslink measurements. Peer reviewers support findings on microtubule detachment kinetics.

Both support conclusion that front-head gating occurs post-ATP binding (C94-C96 overlap with C95-C96). OpenEval notes convergent evidence from multiple approaches. Peer reviewers affirm gating of steps after ATP binding.

Both support control experiments with alternative crosslinking positions (C64-C65, C60). OpenEval emphasizes this validates head-neck linker interaction is critical. Peer reviewers accept controls as supporting main conclusions.

Both support heterodimer configuration establishment (C66-C69, C70-C71). OpenEval emphasizes complementary FRET labeling provides strong evidence. Peer reviewers support experimental design for distinguishing front and rear head properties.

Both support front head measurements in heterodimer (C70-C74 overlap with C72-C74, C94). OpenEval notes ATP binding kinetics similar to unconstrained monomer. Peer reviewers affirm backward-oriented neck linker reduces detachment rates.

Both support heterodimer front head characterization (C70-C71). OpenEval emphasizes similarity to unconstrained monomer supports no backward strain effect on ATP binding. Peer reviewers accept heterodimer design for distinguishing head properties.

Perfect agreement on neck-linker extended heterodimers (C86-C90). Both evaluations support conclusion that orientation rather than tension is primary determinant of front-head gating. Peer reviewers note rear head ATP turnover significantly affected by forward tension.

Both support rear head tension-dependent ATP off-rate (C91-C93). OpenEval emphasizes contrast with front head supports differential gating mechanisms. Peer reviewers confirm rear head ATP turnover affected by degree of forward tension.

Both support alternative crosslinking scheme testing neck-linker docking (C60-C63, C110-C114). OpenEval notes intermediate phenotype supports mechanistic interpretation but conclusion about 'half-opening' is speculative. Peer reviewers support mechanism as consistent with structural data.

Both support alternative crosslinking control (C60). OpenEval emphasizes intermediate phenotype supports neck-linker docking role. Peer reviewers accept control experiments as supporting main conclusions about neck linker-head interactions.

Perfect agreement on structural mechanism involving I325 docking (C110-C114, C61-C63). Both evaluations support interpretation consistent with structural constraints. Peer reviewers note agreement with cryo-EM data, though direct structural validation would strengthen conclusions.

Both support coordination mechanism synthesis (C99-C103, C9). OpenEval emphasizes front head can slowly hydrolyze ATP without neck-linker docking, explaining backward steps. Peer reviewers support detailed kinetic model and note agreement with structural work.

Both support conclusion about rear head ATP release upon front head detachment (C85). OpenEval notes this is consistent with strain-dependent gating mechanism. Peer reviewers support findings on ATP dissociation and strain effects.

Both support main conclusions about asymmetric gating mechanism (C5-C9 overlap with C5-C6, C59, C72-C74, C94). OpenEval notes convergent evidence from all approaches but suggests direct observation of processive movement would strengthen conclusions. Peer reviewers unanimously affirm findings are well-supported.

Both support main conclusions about coordination mechanism (C5-C9 overlap with C9, C99-C103). OpenEval synthesizes results showing asymmetric gating explains coordinated walking. Peer reviewers support detailed kinetic model and mechanistic conclusions.

OpenEval evaluates calculated Kd values showing 5000-fold difference (C97-C98) as UNCERTAIN due to caveats about E236A mutation and Alexa-ATP effects. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific concerns about the magnitude of the difference.

OpenEval supports integration of current results with prior work on backward steps (C104), noting similarity in rates supports interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this comparison to prior backward stepping data.

Peer reviewers accept background claims (C1-C4, C10-C26) as established knowledge providing context. OpenEval results do not separately evaluate these background/introductory claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.
